desc: Formalize the invariant: show the game always ends after exactly K moves where K = (number of non-edges (i,j), i<j, such that adding (i,j) keeps bipartiteness in the final state) and prove K mod 2 is well-defined regardless of move sequence.

Derive the formula: with components having color class sizes (a_c, b_c), total moves K = sum over unordered pairs of vertices not already connected that can ever be connected; compute K mod 2 efficiently from component sizes and M.

Settle whether total-moves parity is play-dependent: confirmed it IS play-dependent (N=4, M=1 example: play lengths 2 vs 3 both terminal). Framework established: N odd → Aoki iff M odd; N even → T ≡ A0 ⊕ F ⊕ M where F is XOR of final flips of odd-sized components; Aoki wants F = 1 ⊕ A0 ⊕ M.

Brute-force all bipartite graphs for N ≤ 5 (selected N=6) with a memoized game solver; fit and verify a closed-form criterion for the N-even flip-control game (who controls F: last-merge player, odd/odd split, filler-move parity interleaving).

Validate the derived criterion against all computed small cases: N=2 M=0 → Aoki; N=3 M=0 → Takahashi; N=3 M=1 → Aoki; N=4 M=0 → Takahashi; N=4 M=1 (edge 12) → Aoki; N=4 M=2 (edges 12,34) → Takahashi; N=4 M=2 (edges 12,13) → Aoki; N=4 M=3 (path) → Aoki; plus samples 1-3.

Prove the fitted criterion rigorously (pairing/strategy argument for who controls F) and reduce to O(N+M): stress-test "(k/2 + f) odd ⟺ Aoki controls F" on randomized N=6 bipartite graphs vs the memoized solver, focusing on many-isolated-vertex configs and configs with large filler counts; if any counterexample appears, refit the rule. [RESULT: rule REFUTED — N=6,M=0 all-isolated gives Takahashi but rule predicts Aoki; isolated-vertex pattern is Aoki wins iff N ≡ 2 mod 4]

Derive the correct criterion: run exhaustive N=6 (all bipartite graphs, using component-multiset canonicalization to make it feasible) and fit the outcome as a function of (k mod 4, f mod 2, A0, M, number of even components with odd a_i, presence of filler in odd components).

Develop the pairing proof: Takahashi's mirror strategy pairs up odd components (pairing their flip bits so F contribution cancels) and pairs filler moves; analyze the residual game on k mod 4 odd components + unpaired filler. Conjecture to test: Aoki wins iff [k ≡ 2 (mod 4) XOR f odd ...] combined with A0⊕M — fit against data.
Special case to nail first: all-isolated N even (answer N ≡ 2 mod 4) — prove via strategy: Aoki's first merge creates an even component; then analyze pairing.
Then update the formula in the code and re-stress on N=6 exhaustive + random N=8 sparse.

Implement DSU with bipartite coloring (parity to root) to find components and their (a_c, b_c) counts, handling up to 2e5 vertices/edges; fix the buggy unused iterative `find`, keep correct recursive `find2` or write a correct iterative parity DSU.
Edge cases: N=1, M=0, isolated vertices, and confirm formula parity matches sample 3.
